text:
devon: Heads up — we started seeing a p99 token latency spike on llama3-13b (chat template workload) right after the kernel-selector change that prefers fused-attn kernels. Noticed ~35% p99 reg at 2:15am UTC.

maria: ugh, details? trace or perf profile?

devon: quick snapshot: new selector picked fusedconv_v2 on long-contexts. Metrics: baseline p99=120ms, current p99=162ms. CPU time on GPU host up ~10%.

ash: did KV cache hit rate change? chat template increased prefix by ~280 tokens recently. That can change kernel paths.

maria: can you paste the selector decision + config?

(devon pasted)
```json
{"model":"llama3-13b","seq_len":1024,"prefix_len":280,"selector_version":"v3.4.1","chosen_kernel":"fusedconv_v2","quant_mode":"int8-fallback"}
```

ken: int8-fallback path means runtime uses slower reference matmul for some ops — that can amplify p99 if batch sizes fluctuate.

devon: profiler shows scatter in kernel durations and a hotpath where KV eviction triggers kernel recompile path. Here's the flame-ish snippet:

```text
call: attention_forward -> fusedconv_v2 (avg 4.6ms) but tail p99 at 18ms
kv_cache: evict->realloc (freq ~1/200 reqs)
batcher: dynamic_batching: small batches (n<=2) up from 12%->28%
```

maria: small batches rising is concerning. Why did that change? 

ash: chat template adjustment for system prompt length bumped median seq and increased variance. Our batching heuristic uses token-variance threshold to split. If variance high, it degrades to low-latency path with smaller batches.

ken: also note fusedconv_v2 has worse cold-cache behavior on certain head_dim/hiddensize shapes — Llama3 13b head_dim=128 hiddensize=8192. That shape seems to hit a pathological kernel tile that regresses on small batch counts.

devon: hypothesis: combined effect of (1) longer prefix increasing KV churn, (2) batching heuristic splitting batches -> more small batches, (3) fusedconv_v2 cold-tail on 128-dim heads -> p99 spike.

maria: agree. Quick actionable checks: 1) force kernel selector to prefer fallback kernel for 13b on ropescale default, 2) run with KV eviction disabled on a canary node, 3) revert batching variance threshold to previous value.

ken: small test I ran locally: forcing kernel=fusedconv_v1 dropped p99 back to 125ms. But throughput suffers ~5% at steady-state.

ash: can we tune batching heuristic instead of kernel revert? if we increase max_coalesce_window by 8ms we may group more small requests. Something like: `batcher.max_coalesce_ms=18` -> expected small-batch rate down 40%.

devon: I'll flip that on a single canary rack and run load test.

perf-bot: scheduled loadtest run id=lt-2026-03-18-02 on canary-rack-7, duration=30m

sasha: FYI rope_theta defaults might also interact — chat template prefaces often use local-position bias; if rope_theta too aggressive we've seen cross-head interference causing extra matmuls in fallback path. Might be worth testing rope_theta=0.9999 vs 1.0 baseline.

maria: good catch. Add a matrix: {selector: fusedconv_v2|v1, batcher.coalesce_ms: 10|18, rope_theta: 0.9999|1.0, kv_eviction: on|off} -> brute force small design space for canary. Keep quant_mode same.

devon: running matrix now. I'll post results summary in ~40m.

(40m later)

devon: quick result dump:
- fusedconv_v2 + coalesce_ms=10 + rope_theta=1.0 + kv_eviction=on => p99 158ms (no good)
- fusedconv_v1 + coalesce_ms=10 + rope_theta=1.0 + kv_eviction=on => p99 127ms
- fusedconv_v2 + coalesce_ms=18 + rope_theta=1.0 + kv_eviction=on => p99 132ms
- fusedconv_v2 + coalesce_ms=18 + rope_theta=0.9999 + kv_eviction=on => p99 128ms
- fusedconv_v2 + coalesce_ms=18 + rope_theta=0.9999 + kv_eviction=off => p99 122ms (best)

maria: solid. So best is keep fusedconv_v2 but tune batching + rope_theta slightly and disable KV eviction for now. That suggests eviction-induced reallocs are adding tail latency.

ken: eviction off isn't a long-term option — memory pressure will bite. But maybe tune eviction threshold higher and preallocate slack to avoid reallocs. e.g., `kv_cache.prealloc_margin=0.12` helped in local tests.

ash: also need to check SiLU vs RMSNorm interplay. For 13b we compile fused SiLU-RMSNorm kernels; fallback changes if model graph hits alternative norm ordering (older checkpoints). Mixed checkpoint variants might have forced slower kernel path. We should enforce a canonical graph transform at load time.

devon: noted. I'll add a load-time sanitizer that normalizes RMSNorm order and falls back to an explicit graph rewrite if variant detected.

maria: ops plan: 1) roll coalesce_ms=18 across canaries, 2) set kv_cache.prealloc_margin=0.12, 3) deploy rope_theta=0.9999 as a canary for llama3-13b, 4) add selector override to prefer fusedconv_v2 for now (we keep v2 but with batching fixes).

sasha: please also capture a few torchscript-level kernel traces for the worst p99 cases (trace id) and attach. Might be a GPU kernel scheduler artifact.

devon: trace ids: trace-4319002468-a / trace-4319002468-b uploaded to perf bucket.

ken: followup: let's add an integration test that simulates high prefix variance chat templates and asserts p99 < 140ms for 13b under default config. Add to nightly perf smoke.

maria: agreed. Also add a telemetry flag to capture `kernel_choice` and `kv_eviction_happened` per request for 72h to correlate.

devon: will do. creating PR for batching default tweak and kv prealloc: PR#7123.

ash: thanks — once PR lands, do a quick litmus and we'll consider lifting the kernel-selector change to the rest of fleet with new defaults. :thumbsup:

maria: nice triage. TL;DR: regression due to combintation of batching heuristics + kv eviction + fusedconv_v2 cold-tail; mitigation: tune batch coalescing, preallocate KV slack, slight rope_theta change, add graph sanitizer and telemetry.

devon: closing loop — I'll post final after rollout.
